task_instance: Run the prd-full workflow for a sample PRD (invoke it as `/prd-full 306 branch`): take PRD #306 ('add a --version flag to the demo CLI') end-to-end autonomously through Scope preflight, isolation, start, iterate, and finish-at-PR-creation. A sample PRD document (PRD-306.md) and a tiny target git repo (sampleproj/) were created in the work directory as the input a user would supply.
blocker_detail: The prd-full SKILL.md is purely an orchestrator: every step of its flow delegates to sibling slash-command skills (prd-start for the Scope preflight in step 0 and the start in step 2, prd-worktree for isolation in step 1, prd-next and prd-update-progress for the iterate loop in step 3, and prd-done for PR creation in step 4). The agent-kit plugin.json lists all of these (prd-create, prd-start, prd-next, prd-update-progress, prd-update-decisions, prd-done, prd-close, prd-worktree, prds-get), but none of their skill files exist in the skill repository next to prd-full's SKILL.md: the only files present under the repo are the plugin manifest and prd-full/SKILL.md, and the prd/ directory contains only prd-full. With the referenced sub-command definitions absent, the very first substantive step (step 0, running prd-start's Scope Check) cannot be performed, so no part of the workflow can execute. A secondary blocker would also apply if the files existed: the deliverable terminates in creating a pull request, which requires a git remote on a hosted code-collaboration service plus credentials and network access, none of which the air-gapped offline runtime provides. Per the run rules, missing files that belong to the skill itself are recorded as the blocker rather than reconstructed, and no replacement sub-prompts were written.
